summary.text:
A small district-council book (£61.5m gross external debt at 31 December 2025) with an unusually short profile: £50m of the £51.5m PWLB — 97% by principal — matures inside 2026. The strategy on page 6 sets out why: the paper prefers to roll short than lock in long, on Arlingclose's 22 December forecast that Bank Rate reaches around 3.25% in 2026. Five months on, Bank Rate is still 3.75% and the DMO's 1-year point sits at 4.03% — above spot, not below.

The three PWLB loans reconcile exactly to our file: PW475884 £1.5m at 8.88% (maturity 2055) + two £25m short-terms at 4.84% and 4.86%, weighted to 4.85% on the nose to match paragraph Bii to the pound. The 8.88% loan is untouchable — today's DMO curve prices the break at £2.2m to redeem £1.5m of principal, a 47% premium.

On the investment side, £20m out to other LAs at 4.15% against £10m in from LAs at 4.05% leaves the council as a small net lender to the local authority market on a ~10bp spread — an uncommon shape. The 2026/27 budget assumes the investment portfolio halves to a £17m average as reserves are used.

Local Government Reorganisation is flagged as an active planning constraint (covering report 2.3): the successor authority will inherit any long-dated positions, which is another reason the paper leans toward short-term rolls only.

officer.subject: £50m of your PWLB rolls this year — 97% of the book
officer.body:
Hi Brian,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts on the treasury strategy Full Council approved on 4 March. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Your paper is clear and well laid out and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

As a cross-check that our numbers tie to yours, we hold three PWLB loans for East Herts totalling £51.5m and both tranches in your Appendix Bii tie exactly. The £1.5m long-term at 8.875% is one loan maturing 1 February 2055. The £50m short-term at 4.85% is two £25m tranches — one at 4.84%, one at 4.86% — weighting to 4.85% to the basis point. You can see it all at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

Which means £50m of your £51.5m PWLB — 97% — matures inside 2026. Paragraph 6 of the strategy sets out why: you'd rather roll short than lock in long, and that rests on the Arlingclose forecast on page 3 (22 December) that Bank Rate reaches around 3.25% in 2026. Five months on, Bank Rate is still 3.75%, and the short end of the market curve now sits a little above spot rather than below it. The premise is testable in real time — one of the two shorts matured in June, and the other matures this week — and we hold both sides of it.

The 8.875% loan is the other end of the same book. Priced today against the DMO's premature repayment curve, it would cost roughly £2.2m to redeem the £1.5m balance — a 47% premium — so it's cheaper to run to 2055 than to touch. We flag it because it's the highest surviving PWLB rate on your book by a distance, worth being visible on the profile even where nothing is actionable. Break costs are indicative only; the DMO's quote is the only binding one.

On the investment side, the £20m out to other authorities at 4.15% against £10m in from LAs at 4.05% is a small but uncommon shape — most councils sit clearly on one side of the LA market, not both. Our monthly sector view at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity carries where the LA market is settling each month; useful when a roll comes up.

None of it needs a meeting or a subscription, and the rates page at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard takes ten seconds to check. On training, three look most relevant to East Herts: Interest rate risk, for the short-term concentration; Strategic PWLB borrowing, for when the roll decisions come around; and our liability benchmark pathway, which is interactive and built on live data — worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
